concepts.def: Adjustable opening in the lens controlling light intake and depth of field, measured in f-stops such as f/1.8 or f/16.
Duration the sensor or film is exposed to light, determining motion blur or freezing, measured in fractions of a second.
Sensitivity of the sensor or film to light, with higher values enabling low-light shooting but adding grain or noise.
Range of distance appearing acceptably sharp in an image, controlled by aperture, focal length and subject distance.
Arrangement of visual elements within the frame, using devices such as the rule of thirds, leading lines and framing.
Henri Cartier-Bresson's concept of the perfect split-second capturing the essence of an event, central to documentary photography.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Photography — a core area of A-Level Art & Design.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Photography brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Photography.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.
